hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Both plugins keep the locally-installed insrc daemon current over ONE net-new daemon-owned update+restart IPC. The daemon exposes a single request that pulls, rebuilds and self-restarts by spawning a DETACHED helper (the proven daemon-ctl.sh update+restart sequence) — the only safe way a process respawns itself, since the request's own socket dies mid-restart. Freshness is judged purely by git-commit comparison: the daemon reports its installed source commit additively on the existing daemon.status; each plugin runs a remote git ls-remote (no pull) against the daemon repo's default branch and compares. On drift the startup path shows a native in-IDE notification (Update/Dismiss) and updates only on approval; a plugin self-update triggers the daemon update automatically (notify-after, fire-and-forget). Failure surfaces once with the raw error; no retry/rollback — the daemon owns its state. The plugin confirms success by reconnecting and re-reading the installed commit.

ownedContracts.name: DaemonStatus.installedCommit
ownedContracts.purpose: The additive freshness anchor on the existing daemon.status object: the daemon's currently-installed source commit, compared by each plugin against the upstream default-branch commit (k1) with no version scheme introduced.

boundary.internal: How the daemon computes its installed commit (running git rev-parse HEAD against the daemon root under the ~/.insrc home, caching vs re-reading, and the best-effort fallback to "" when the working copy is unavailable) stays private to s2. Consumers see only the installedCommit string on daemon.status; the never-throw best-effort guarantee of daemon.status is preserved.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The detached-helper mechanism itself is private to s1: how the daemon spawns daemon-ctl.sh update+restart fully detached (its own session/process group so it survives the daemon exit), where and how the DaemonUpdateOutcome record is persisted under the daemon home, and how the restarted daemon reads that record on boot to surface it. Callers see only the sc1 method shape — launch acknowledgement plus the reconnect-and-read-outcome protocol — never the helper wiring or the daemon-ctl.sh invocation details.

Everything VS-Code-specific stays private to s3: the activation hook that runs the check opportunistically only when the daemon is already reachable (k6), the remote git ls-remote invocation and commit comparison, the showInformationMessage notification with inline Update/Dismiss (k7), the first-activation detection that distinguishes a plugin self-update from an ordinary startup (to pick the approval-prompt path vs the auto notify-after path, k4), the fire-and-forget scheduling so the daemon update never blocks the plugin's own startup, and the reconnect-and-confirm loop plus the single failure notification (k5). None of this is consumed by any other Story.

Everything JetBrains-specific stays private to s4: the postStartupActivity hook running the opportunistic-when-reachable check (k6), the ls-remote comparison, the insrc Notifications BALLOON with inline Update/Dismiss (k7), the plugin-version-change detection that selects the approval path vs the auto notify-after self-update path (k4), the fire-and-forget scheduling off the UI thread so it never blocks activation, and the reconnect-and-confirm plus single failure balloon (k5). It mirrors s3's behaviour by consuming the same sc1 + sc2 contracts; it shares no code with s3.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase A — daemon foundations (update+restart IPC and installed-commit report)

nonFunctional.performance: The startup check must add negligible latency to activation: the daemon.status read reuses the existing connection and the ls-remote is a single lightweight network round-trip run off the activation-blocking path (fire-and-forget), so a slow or unreachable network never stalls plugin startup. daemon.status remains best-effort and must not become slower — installedCommit is a cheap local git read.
nonFunctional.security: No new network surface beyond the plugin's ls-remote against the already-trusted daemon repo remote; the update executes only local, already-installed code (daemon-ctl.sh) under the user's account. No cloud REST is introduced. The update runs only on explicit approval (startup path) or as a consequence of the user having installed a new plugin version (self-update path).
nonFunctional.observability: The update outcome (succeeded/failed + raw error) is persisted by the daemon and surfaced to the plugin after reconnect, and the plugin renders exactly one notification per outcome (k5). The installed commit is always readable via daemon.status for after-the-fact freshness inspection.
nonFunctional.durability: The daemon owns its own post-update state: a failed update leaves the daemon in whatever state the failure produced with no rollback (k5). The DaemonUpdateOutcome record persists across the restart so the reconnecting plugin can read a terminal result even though the triggering socket was severed.

api.name: daemon.status

returns.meaning: The existing status snapshot, now carrying one additive field installedCommit:string — the daemon root's current git HEAD sha, or '' when undeterminable. Every other field is unchanged; the handler remains best-effort/never-throws.

postconditions: The returned DaemonStatus.installedCommit is the trimmed full sha of `git rev-parse HEAD` against DAEMON_ROOT, or '' when the root is absent / not a git repo / git unavailable.
daemon.status still never throws: the git read is wrapped best-effort, exactly like the existing LMDB-size fs stat, so a git failure degrades to '' and does not fail the status call.
No other DaemonStatus field is changed and sc1 (daemon.update/updateOutcome) is not touched.

api.name: readInstalledCommit
api.signature: readInstalledCommit(root?: string, deps?: { exec?: (cmd: string, args: readonly string[]) => string }): string

parameters.name: root
parameters.purpose: The daemon checkout root to read HEAD from; defaults to $INSRC_DAEMON_ROOT ?? ~/.insrc/daemon (the tree daemon-ctl.sh updates).

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: Injected exec seam (default: execFileSync-based git runner) so the reader is unit-testable without a real git process.

returns.meaning: The trimmed full HEAD sha (`git rev-parse HEAD` of root), or '' on any failure — non-git/missing root, git absent, or a thrown exec. Never throws.

postconditions: Pure + side-effect-free apart from the read-only git exec; returns '' rather than throwing on every failure path (best-effort), so daemon.status's never-throw contract holds.
Runs `git -C <root> rev-parse HEAD` (the same command daemon-ctl.sh uses for its 'current' commit) — a cheap local read, no network, no version scheme (k1).

It is a plain string ('' when undeterminable) rather than optional, so consumers can always read it; existing fields and the never-throw guarantee are unchanged. interactionWithShared.howDetails: S002 owns and realizes sc2 (DaemonStatus.installedCommit). The additive installedCommit:string field on DaemonStatus is the contract surface both s3 and s4 consume; the daemon.status handler populates it from the pure readInstalledCommit() helper (best-effort git rev-parse HEAD of DAEMON_ROOT, '' when undeterminable). How the commit is computed — the reader module, DAEMON_ROOT resolution, and the '' fallback — is s2-internal; consumers see only the string. daemon.status's never-throw guarantee is preserved, and sc1 (daemon.update/updateOutcome, S001) is NOT touched.

errorCases.scenario: The daemon root is not a git repository (or does not exist) — e.g. a tarball/zip install, or a dev daemon whose ~/.insrc/daemon is absent
errorCases.detection: `git -C <root> rev-parse HEAD` exits non-zero / throws (execFileSync raises on a non-zero exit), which readInstalledCommit catches in its try/catch.
errorCases.response: readInstalledCommit returns '' ; daemon.status sets installedCommit:'' and returns normally. The handler never throws.
errorCases.userImpact: The plugin sees installedCommit:'' and treats it as 'freshness undeterminable' — skips the drift check silently (per the plugin flows, adjacent boundary), never an error.

errorCases.scenario: git is not installed / not on PATH
errorCases.detection: spawning `git` fails with ENOENT; execFileSync throws, caught by readInstalledCommit's try/catch.
errorCases.response: Return '' ; daemon.status carries installedCommit:'' and still returns the rest of the status normally.
errorCases.userImpact: Same as a non-git root — freshness undeterminable, check skipped; no crash, no degraded status.

errorCases.scenario: The git command hangs or is unexpectedly slow
errorCases.detection: N/A at correctness level — `git rev-parse HEAD` is a local plumbing read with no network; there is no expected hang. (A pathological slow FS is out of scope; the exec is bounded by git's own local read.)
errorCases.response: The synchronous read completes as any local git plumbing call; if git itself errored it falls to the '' path above. No new timeout machinery is introduced for a cheap local read.
errorCases.userImpact: daemon.status latency is one local git exec (a few ms) — within the nonFunctional 'cheap local git read' budget; not a hot path.

edgeCases.input: A detached-HEAD daemon root (checked out at a commit, not a branch)
edgeCases.expected: `git rev-parse HEAD` still returns the current commit sha — installedCommit is the exact build commit, which is precisely what the freshness comparison needs (k1 compares commits, not branches).

edgeCases.input: A dirty working tree (uncommitted local edits) under the daemon root
edgeCases.expected: installedCommit is the HEAD commit sha, unaffected by uncommitted changes — the reader reports the installed BUILD commit, not working-tree state.

edgeCases.input: readInstalledCommit called with no root argument
edgeCases.expected: Resolves DAEMON_ROOT = $INSRC_DAEMON_ROOT ?? ~/.insrc/daemon and reads HEAD there — the tree the daemon runs from / daemon-ctl.sh updates.

edgeCases.input: git stdout carries a trailing newline (and rev-parse prints the full 40-char sha)
edgeCases.expected: The reader .trim()s the output so installedCommit is the bare sha with no surrounding whitespace.

alternativesConsidered.name: Per-read best-effort git read via a pure helper
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: daemon.status computes installedCommit on every read by calling a pure readInstalledCommit(root) helper (synchronous best-effort git rev-parse HEAD), falling back to '' — no caching, no daemon lifecycle state.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add installedCommit:string to DaemonStatus (src/shared/types.ts) and set it in the daemon.status handler (index.ts:922) from a new pure module (e.g. src/daemon/installed-commit.ts) exporting readInstalledCommit(root, deps?) over an injected exec seam. The reader runs `git -C <root> rev-parse HEAD` (execFileSync, encoding utf8), trims the sha, and returns '' on any failure (non-git root, git absent, exec throw) — all inside try/catch so it never throws. root resolves as $INSRC_DAEMON_ROOT ?? ~/.insrc/daemon, the same tree daemon-ctl.sh updates. Called per status read, mirroring the handler's existing per-read best-effort fs stat (LMDB size).
pros: Simplest + most obviously correct: the field always reflects the current git HEAD of the daemon root, with no cache-invalidation reasoning
Consistent with daemon.status's existing idiom — it already recomputes per read (uptime, queue depth, the LMDB-size fs stat) and wraps best-effort reads in try/catch
No new daemon lifecycle state / boot hook — the pure helper is trivially unit-testable over an injected exec seam
Robust to any out-of-band git change under the daemon root (e.g. a manual checkout) since it reads live each time
cons: Runs one local `git rev-parse HEAD` per status read — a few ms of blocking exec, though status is not a hot path and the HLD calls this a cheap local read
The exec cost repeats even though the commit only actually changes across a restart

alternativesConsidered.name: Compute once at daemon boot, cache in memory
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Resolve installedCommit ONCE during daemon startup, store it in a module/scope variable, and return the cached value on every status read — zero per-read cost.
alternativesConsidered.approach: During daemon setup, call readInstalledCommit(root) once and hold the result in the daemon scope (or a module singleton). daemon.status returns the cached string. Because a self-update RESTARTS the daemon (sc1), the fresh process recomputes at its own boot, so the cached value is always correct for the process lifetime — the installed commit is invariant within a running daemon.
pros: Zero per-read cost — daemon.status stays exactly as fast as today (just returns a captured string)
Correct for the domain invariant: the installed commit changes only across a restart, and a restart re-boots the daemon
The pure reader is still injected + unit-testable; only the call site moves to boot
cons: Introduces daemon lifecycle state (a cached field wired at startup) — more surface than a1's stateless per-read
Goes stale if the daemon root's git HEAD changes WITHOUT a restart (an unusual manual git op on the running tree), unlike a1's live read
Slightly more to test (the boot wiring + the cache), not just the pure reader
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Also satisfies ac1/sc2/k1 and is strictly cheaper per read (returns a cached string), but buys that with daemon lifecycle state (a boot hook + cache) and a staleness caveat if the root's HEAD changes without a restart — more surface than a1 for a saving the HLD already deems unnecessary (the read is cheap). A close second, preferable only if status becomes a hot path.

alternativesConsidered.name: Lazy memoize on first status read
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Compute installedCommit on the first daemon.status read and cache it for subsequent reads — a hybrid: no boot cost, no repeated exec.
alternativesConsidered.approach: daemon.status calls readInstalledCommit(root) only the first time (guarded by a nullable cache in the daemon scope), memoizes the result, and returns the cache thereafter. Combines a1's no-boot-hook simplicity with a2's amortized zero-cost reads.
pros: No boot-time work if daemon.status is never called; amortizes the single git exec across all later reads
Keeps the pure reader injected + testable
cons: Same staleness caveat as a2 (a post-first-read git change under the root is not reflected), but with a less predictable capture point (whenever the first status read happens to land — possibly before an install settles)
Adds a nullable-cache guard for a saving (one git exec) the HLD already deems cheap — complexity not clearly worth it
Capturing at 'first read' is a fuzzier moment than a1's 'every read' or a2's 'at boot'
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Satisfies ac1/k1 but only partial on sc2's spirit: it adds a nullable-cache guard AND inherits the staleness caveat, with a less predictable capture moment than either a1 (every read) or a2 (boot) — the most machinery for the least clarity, saving one git exec the HLD already calls cheap.
